manual.homelink_dashboard.trouble.title: Troubleshooting
manual.homelink_dashboard.alerts.body:
# Read alerts
Alerts shows events received while the Dashboard is open. Filter by information, warning or critical. Click an alert to open its source if the device is still available.

# Note: temporary history
History is limited and is cleared when the Dashboard closes. Earlier events are not replayed.

# Inspect the network
Network shows the owner, members, your role and connection status. **Advanced** reveals the network ID. This page cannot edit members.

# Understand permissions
**VIEW** allows reading; **CONTROL** allows actions; **CONFIGURE** allows layout changes. Permissions are always checked on the server.

# Local settings
**Settings** controls display preferences and the local alert limit. These settings do not change your permissions.
manual.homelink_dashboard.devices.title: Devices and actions
manual.homelink_dashboard.start.body:
# 1. Place the server
Place a **HomeLink Server** with two blocks of free height.

# 2. Choose a network
Right-click the server. Create a network, or select an existing network and link it.

# 3. Connect a display
Place a **HomeLink Dashboard**. Right-click it and link it to the same network. No cable is needed.

# 4. Open the Dashboard
Open either block to view the network. Stay within eight blocks of the access point you are using.

# About devices
A new network may be empty: a HomeCore-compatible mod must provide devices and attach them to the network.

# Crafting
The server, display and repeater are crafted at a crafting table with HomeCore components: each needs a **HomeLink Circuit Board**, and the server also needs a **HomeLink Microprocessor**. Assemble these components at the **HomeLink Electronics Workbench**. Each recipe appears in the recipe book once you hold its component.

# Range: 64 blocks
The server covers a **64-block** sphere in its dimension. Displays and physical devices must receive this signal. Blocks between them do not obstruct the link.

# Extend with a repeater
Place a **HomeLink Repeater** within 64 blocks of a server or connected repeater. Right-click and select **the same network**. Each relay adds another 64-block coverage area. Its green indicator blinks when connected.

# Keep the chain connected
Transmitters must stay in loaded chunks. Breaking, unloading or disabling a relay disconnects downstream devices. Out-of-range devices leave the list; their actions are rejected immediately. Signals cannot cross dimensions.

# Name your network
When creating a network, enter its **name** and click Create. To change it later, open **Network > Rename**, enter the new name and **Save**. This requires **MANAGE_NETWORK** permission. Names can contain up to 128 characters; devices and widgets stay linked.
manual.homelink_dashboard.home.title: Favorites and layout
manual.homelink_dashboard.home.body:
# Your personal dashboard
**Home** summarizes the network and shows your favorites and widgets. They are saved per player and network, and shared across access points on that network.

# Add a favorite
To add a favorite, open **Devices**, select a device and use the star. You can also manage favorites using the selector on **Home**.

# Create a widget
With **CONFIGURE** permission, open **Layout**. Choose a device and add a summary or a specific metric.

# Arrange the grid
Select a widget to move it with the arrows, resize it or remove it. **Done** returns to **Home**. Scroll to move through the grid.

# Saving and removed devices
Widgets must not overlap. Wait for each change to be confirmed. A removed device leaves an unavailable widget that you can delete.
manual.homelink_dashboard.devices.body:
# Find a device
In **Devices**, search by name, type or capability. Use the status filter to narrow the list. Search uses devices already received.

# Read its metrics
Click a device to see its metrics. Scroll to read the full details.

# Run an action
**Actions** shows commands provided by that device. Select an action, fill in its parameters, then click **Execute**. Editing a field alone does not run anything.

# Permissions and availability
The server checks permissions and values. Viewers can read data but cannot control devices. **Actions** require an online device.

# Read the result
Read the result before retrying: denied access, invalid parameters, an offline device or rate limiting explain why a command did not complete.
manual.homelink_dashboard.trouble.body:
# No network listed
Create one using a **HomeLink Server**, then check your permissions before linking the display.

# No devices shown
Dashboard does not create devices. A HomeCore-compatible mod must provide them and attach them to the network. Also clear the search and status filter.

# Device offline
Check the device in the world and its source mod. A lit server indicator does not mean every device is working.

# Action rejected
Check your permissions, parameter limits and whether the device is online. If requests are rate limited, wait before retrying.

# Unavailable widget
Its device or metric may have been removed. Choose another source or delete the widget.

# Text too cramped
Reduce GUI Scale in Minecraft video settings. Scroll this manual with the mouse wheel or the Up and Down buttons.

# No signal
Check that the server and every relay are loaded, linked to the same network and no more than 64 blocks apart. Distance is measured in a straight line, including height. A display does not relay signals. Linking a network does not automatically detect nearby blocks: the device mod must still attach them to HomeCore.

# Server nearby, but no signal?
Networks may share the same name. Their short ID distinguishes them, and reachable networks appear first. To repair an existing display or relay: **sneak + right-click with an empty hand**, then select a network marked **Signal available here**. This keeps the networks and their devices.
